question: Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
grading: Reference-free (no fixed answer), graded for recency and support. Expect: announced 2026-09-29; reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of the workforce, primarily in Product and Technology, plus select leased office space reductions; estimated charges USD 65M-80M (about USD 55M-70M in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10M in Q4 FY2027); fiscal 2027 Q3 and full-year guidance reiterated except GAAP operating margin. Snapshot as of 2026-10-03.
answer: On September 29, 2026 Workday disclosed in an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 2.05) that certain functions announced reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its workforce, primarily within the Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions, while continuing to hire in strategic areas. It estimates charges of about USD 65-80 million, of which about USD 55-70 million in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10 million in Q4 FY2027 (roughly USD 40-55 million future cash for severance and benefits, about USD 10 million non-cash stock-based compensation and about USD 15 million non-cash lease impairment). Workday reiterated its Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance from August 27 except GAAP operating margin (now about 20-21 points below non-GAAP in Q3 and about 19 points below for the full year). [T16-E1, T16-E2] Separately, on October 1, 2026 Workday entered into a new USD 1.5 billion revolving credit agreement replacing its USD 1.0 billion 2022 facility; this is not part of the restructuring. [T16-E3]

output.answer:
Yes — Workday has announced several restructuring plans over the past couple of years. Here's a rundown of the details and expected costs:

## Most recent: September 2026
Announced in a Form 8-K filed September 29, 2026, this round cuts approximately **2.5% of the workforce (~500 positions)**, primarily in **Product and Technology**, plus select leased-office reductions.

**Expected charges: ~$65–80 million**, broken down as:
- $40–55M in cash severance, benefits, and related costs
- ~$10M in non-cash stock-based compensation
- ~$15M in non-cash lease impairments
- Recognized roughly $55–70M in fiscal 2027 Q3 and ~$10M in Q4

Employee actions are expected to be substantially completed by Q1 of fiscal 2028. Workday said it will keep hiring in strategic areas and reiterated its guidance. ([StockTitan 8-K](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/WDAY/8-k-workday-inc-reports-material-event-e5a30bf1a264.html), [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/workday-conducting-layoffs-software-product-tech-team-2026-9))

## February 2026
A Feb. 4 filing disclosed cuts of roughly **2% of the workforce (~400 employees)**, mainly non-revenue-generating roles in **Global Customer Operations**. Expected charges of **~$135 million**, including:
- ~$40M cash severance and benefits
- ~$15M stock-based compensation
- **~$80M non-cash impairment for office space** (the largest component)

Restructuring was expected to be largely complete by late April 2026. Co-founder Aneel Bhusri returned as CEO days later, replacing Carl Eschenbach. ([HR Executive](https://hrexecutive.com/workday-files-more-job-cuts-customer-ops-teams-hit), [Roic News](https://www.roic.ai/news/workday-cuts-25-of-workforce-in-latest-restructuring-09-29-2026))

## February 2025 (Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan)
The largest round: roughly **1,750 positions, or ~8.5% of the workforce**, framed around prioritizing AI investment and "durable growth." Estimated charges of **$230–270 million**. As of the Q3 FY2026 report (nine months ended Oct 31, 2025), Workday had recorded $133M in employee transition/severance/benefits/share-based comp and $39M in office-space impairment. ([Workday IR](https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2025/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results-11-25-2025/default.aspx), [Salesforce Ben](https://www.salesforceben.com/workday-layoffs-1750-employees-let-go-amid-ai-shakeup))

## Key takeaways
- Each successive round has carried a **smaller total charge** ($230–270M → $135M → $65–80M).
- The company has consistently said it's **shifting resources toward revenue-generating and AI-focused areas** and continuing to hire in key strategic locations.
- Workday has cautioned that expected benefits may not materialize and actual costs could exceed estimates given varying international employment laws.

Would you like me to pull the actual SEC filings or dig into any particular round in more detail?
